name: Rehum
overview: Rehum is a male figure known primarily as the commander who authored a letter opposing the people of Judah during the post-exilic period. His tribal affiliation and further personal details are not recorded in Scripture. His role is noted specifically in the context of opposition against the rebuilding efforts in Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Rehum means '[he] is compassionate,' though this meaning is not explicitly connected to his actions. The name is a proper name and is not indicated to have been given by God. This is the only recorded name for this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Rehum beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as a commander who wrote against Judah. No additional relational information is provided.
scriptureSignificance: Rehum's significance lies in his leadership role as a commander who actively opposed the restoration of Judah after the exile. His written opposition reflects the challenges faced by the returning exiles in rebuilding their community and temple. Through his actions, Rehum represents the external resistance to God's providential plan for His people during this critical period.
